fixes.explanation: Armies it is, friend. Jabin, king of Hazor, sent word to the other kings, and they "…came out with all their armies, a multitude as numerous as the sand on the seashore…" (Joshua 11:1, 4). ONE message went out, and look at that turnout! I can't even get everybody to answer one group text.

The Valley of Elah belongs to a whole other story, where Saul, Israel's king, and the men of Israel camped to face the Philistines (1 Samuel 17:2). Here, Joshua 11:5 says the kings joined forces and encamped at the waters of Merom. Two camps, two stories. It's easy to mix them up, so no crumbs to be embarrassed about.

True, baker! The LORD told Joshua to hamstring the horses and burn up the chariots (Joshua 11:6). Then verse 9 says Joshua treated them as the LORD had told him. No tweaking, no "close enough." I've been known to eyeball the flour and call it a day, so this kind of follow-through impresses me.

Gaza, Gath and Ashdod, baker! Verse 22 says no Anakim were left in the land of the Israelites, "…only in Gaza, Gath, and Ashdod did any survive." Verse 21 has Joshua clearing them out of the hill country, and then this little list is all that's left. Three cities. You picked them out like a pro.

Careful, friend, those names come from the verse right before. Verse 21 says Joshua eliminated the Anakim from the hill country of Hebron, Debir and Anab. The survivors come in verse 22: Gaza, Gath and Ashdod. Two verses back to back, like two cookie tins that look the same. You just grabbed the wrong tin.

Jericho, Ai and Bethel are good, famous names, but they aren't in this part of the story. Joshua 11:22 says the Anakim who survived were in Gaza, Gath and Ashdod. Famous isn't the same as listed, friend. I learned that one the hard way in the back of a drawer.
